subject: Attribution & Update Policy — RFI response (Delta Financial Services)
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@deltafin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Model attribution, provenance & update notifications

Rishi —

Thanks for taking our RFI. We're compiling a formal comparison across vendors and Delta's legal and platform teams have a few specific questions about how Redwood treats open-model licenses, provenance metadata, and model updates. Short bullet list we need answers for (we'll follow up with additional items if needed):

1) License inventory: do you track the license (OSI/other) for every model and component in your catalog? Provide a CSV or machine-readable manifest format.

2) Provenance chain: what metadata do you capture for each model build (base model, weights hash, training dataset provenance, fine-tune recipe, tokenizer version)? How immutable is that record once published?

3) Version pinning & update notifications: can customers pin to a specific model artifact (hash/version) and opt out of automatic updates? If you push a security/quality patch to a hosted model, what is your notification SLA and can customers delay rollouts?

4) Attribution obligations: for models with third-party or community licenses, what obligations do you surface to customers (e.g., required notices, citation text)?

5) Compatibility & license conflict scanning: do you scan customer-provided fine-tuning data or integrated third-party modules for license conflicts?

If you can send a short technical appendix and a cover note from your legal/commercial team that addresses these items, that would be ideal. We hope to close this RFI by 2026-12-22.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Rao
Sr. Procurement Manager — Delta Financial Services
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@deltafin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Model attribution, provenance & update notifications

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached: a short technical appendix (redwood-model-licensing-appendix.pdf) and a machine-friendly provenance CSV (model-provenance-structure.csv). High level answers inline below; please see attachments for the formal format we can ingest into your vendor evaluation system.

1) License inventory: Yes — every model in our public catalog has an associated license field (SPDX or equivalent). For composed artifacts (e.g., base model + finetune), we emit a merged license vector and flag incompatibilities. Attachment: licensing appendix (CSV excerpt).

2) Provenance chain: We capture base model identifier, weights SHA256, training dataset identifiers (when available), tokenizer version, fine-tune script hash, and evaluation snapshot IDs. This metadata is stored immutably in our catalog service once a model artifact is published; updates create a new artifact record with an explicit parent pointer.

3) Version pinning & updates: Customers can pin to an exact artifact by SHA or semantic version. For hosted inference, the default for new deployments is to use a named model alias (e.g., stable/latest) but pinning is available at the deployment/route level. For security patches we have a staged rollout: we notify customers via email + Console alert at least 72 hours before a non-security breaking update, and for high-severity security fixes we provide emergency notifications and an opt-in forced patch unless a contractual pin prevents automatic updates. We can include a pinning SLA in Dedicated/Private contracts.

4) Attribution obligations: For models derived from third-party weights or datasets with attribution clauses, we include a "required notices" block in the model detail page and in the manifest. We provide suggested citation text and sample license headers customers can display.

5) Compatibility scanning: We run an automated license compatibility check on models we publish; we do not (by default) scan customer training data for license conflicts unless customers enable our data-review service as part of onboarding (this is an add-on).

Next steps — I've looped in Neha (policy) and will pull legal language for an addendum. If you want, we can produce a one-page executive cover note and a short clause you can insert in your vendor addendum describing pinning and notification timelines.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-model-licensing-appendix.pdf (6 pages), model-provenance-structure.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFI: Model attribution, provenance & update notifications — need legal + policy wording

Team — forwarding Delta's RFI and my draft replies. They specifically asked for: (a) machine-readable license manifest (done), (b) immutable provenance record description (done), and (c) contractual wording for pinning + notification SLA.

Questions for legal/compliance:
- Can we offer a standard 72-hour notification window for non-critical updates and an emergency patch workflow for CVEs?
- For Dedicated and Private customers can we state that pinned artifacts will not be automatically upgraded without customer consent? (I believe we can)
- Draft a concise addendum clause that mentions: artifact SHA pinning, notification timelines, and a "pin-hold" option that prevents automated rollouts for 90 days unless customer approves earlier.

I've attached a draft pinning policy (redwood-pinning-policy-draft.docx). Can you review and reply with redlines by EOD Dec 10? Delta needs an answer before their procurement close date (Dec 22).

Thanks — R
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Model attribution, provenance & update notifications — need legal + policy wording

Rishi —

Reviewed the draft. TL;DR: we can provide the requested commitments with the following safe, contract-ready language. Please use this text for the one-page addendum and the RFI cover note.

Proposed addendum clause (suggested):
"Redwood Inference shall provide customers with manifest-level provenance for any served model artifact, including base model identifier, artifact hash (SHA256), tokenizer version, and recorded fine-tune recipe. Provenance records are immutable: any modification results in the publication of a new artifact with an explicit parent reference. Customers may pin service routes to a specific artifact SHA or semantic version. Redwood will not automatically modify pinned artifacts. For non-security updates to non-pinned artifacts Redwood will provide at least seventy-two (72) hours' notice before rollout. For high-severity security patches Redwood may perform an emergency rollout; Redwood will provide expedited notice and remediation guidance and will honor explicit contractual pin-hold requests for up to ninety (90) days pending customer approval."
Comments:
- We should avoid promising rollback windows for customer code; keep scope limited to artifact publication and rollout notices.
- For Hosted customers add a sentence referencing Console UI and API hooks for pin management and notification subscriptions.
- Karthik, please confirm whether the 90-day pin-hold is operationally feasible for Dedicated capacity (I think yes with a ticketed override).

I'll convert to legal-ready PDF and Rishi — can you send the executive cover note to Maya after I finalize?

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference

Rishi / Laura —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. The proposed addendum language looks good to our legal team in principle; they asked for two small clarifications before we move to a DocuSign addendum: (1) explicit mention that the provenance CSV includes the SHA256 for both base weights and derived artifact (we see it in your sample but want it in the clause), and (2) confirmation that the "notification" channels include both email and Console alerts (not just email).

If you can send a one-paragraph executive cover note (2–3 sentences) and a DocuSign-ready PDF, we can start procurement. Our legal contact is attached on this thread.

Thanks,
Maya
